cards.hint: Recall how the purchase changed national scale.
cards.quote: For roughly 4 cents an acre, the United States doubled its size, expanding the nation westward.
cards.stem: What was the effect of this purchase on the size of the nation?

cards.hint: Think about total price, not per acre cost.
cards.quote: signed on April 30, 1803, the United States purchased 828,000 square miles of land west of the Mississippi River for $15 million.
cards.stem: How much did the United States pay in this transaction with France?

cards.hint: Remember the two men sent to buy New Orleans.
options: Treaty of Cession and two conventions
cards.quote: negotiators Robert Livingston and James Monroe were authorized to pay France up to $10 million
cards.stem: Who were the original negotiators authorized to buy New Orleans?

cards.hint: Focus on North and South tensions.
cards.quote: also exposed the sectional weaknesses between the North and South, especially related to the issue of slavery.
cards.stem: What sectional division did each expansion expose?
